**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Query NAIP coverage when manually selected**

When the camera was moved while a source such as EOX or OSM was selected, choosing `usgs-naip` only calls `select()`. Since that view has no cached footprint, `desired()` immediately substitutes EOX, while the only path that calls `queryFootprint()` is the camera `moveEnd` handler in `updateView()` and no new camera event occurs. The manual NAIP choice therefore remains stuck on EOX until the user moves the camera again; route this selection through the footprint-query path before finalizing the fallback.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The owner has explicitly replaced the manual-source UX with automatic best-available imagery. The source/Auto selector, persisted manual preference and source Retry are removed.

The underlying stationary-camera bug is corrected: initialization now runs the same automatic coverage path as settled camera updates. One budgeted JSON-point request qualifies a genuine footprint; healthy global imagery remains during qualification. Camera/selection generation, controller epoch and teardown reject stale results. A verified partial footprint is cached for a later closer view but cannot activate NAIP until the whole view is covered. Missing/timeout/source-failure cases retain truthful fallback; eligible cooldown recovery is automatic and bounded. Public MapSourceController switching/caches remain in use.

Verification: 17 controller regressions execute the actual pinned controller, including stationary/valid/unavailable/timeout/source-failure/late-result/shared-budget and automatic recovery cases; installed-browser stationary native-NAIP fixture passes. All 11 bounded desktop/mobile browser cases pass. Live matching-scale captures and remaining provider/timing limits are recorded in docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md under C6-1A automatic imagery correction. No provider limit was widened, and no manual choice is needed.

Corrected and verified at `27b0d2af9e8bba8372656f376435fb8e0e78d95b`; final Earth artifact `bdfa4089e0ab3d77fa3f987e1a02c3f2b7fd7896f8f4804e439a762f1600c042`. NAIP close NYC visibly renders real detail but is still loading at the bounded120s capture; that performance/visual gate stays open. PR remains unmerged for owner review.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the mobile imagery panel clear of selection controls**

On standalone viewports below 600 px, the expanded imagery panel is anchored at `bottom:84px` with up to 36% viewport height and `z-index:3`, while the existing selected-object panel is anchored at `bottom:90px` with `z-index:2`. Whenever an object is selected, these panels occupy the same lower-right region, so the imagery panel obscures selection details and controls such as Stop tracking; collapse or reposition one panel when the other is active.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The owner-directed automatic UX removes the conflicting imagery-selection panel entirely, including its mobile positioning and source/Auto, Retry and labels controls. A small read-only source/quality disclosure shares the attribution footer. Hub diagnostics no longer asks users to retry imagery; independent event/layer controls are preserved.

Verified on the installed final Earth artifact at 390×844 standalone and embedded: real declared satellite fixtures show details; Focus, Track and Stop Tracking execute and report the actual tracking state; source status/credits and navigation remain accessible. Standalone selection/footer rectangles do not overlap. Matching screenshots include mobile-standalone-selection.png, mobile-embedded-details.png and mobile-embedded-selection.png in the local owner gallery. Both narrow-view regressions and all 11 bounded browser cases pass. This is software Chromium fixture proof, not physical-device qualification.

Corrected and verified at `27b0d2af9e8bba8372656f376435fb8e0e78d95b`; final Earth artifact `bdfa4089e0ab3d77fa3f987e1a02c3f2b7fd7896f8f4804e439a762f1600c042`. NAIP close NYC visibly renders real detail but is still loading at the bounded120s capture; that performance/visual gate stays open. PR remains unmerged for owner review.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reopen footprint queries after a 429 cooldown**

When the NAIP footprint endpoint returns 429, this branch blocks `imagery.nationalmap.gov` and returns, but it never adds `usgs-naip` to `failedSources`. Because `needsUpdate()`/`recoverEligible()` only call `retryHost()` while iterating failed sources, the expired block is never removed; `canQueryFootprint()` continues seeing NAIP as ineligible, so every later covered U.S. view remains on EOX until the runtime is recreated. Register this failure for automatic recovery or otherwise expire the metadata-host block after Retry-After.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L972-L973](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/27b0d2af9e8bba8372656f376435fb8e0e78d95b/AGENTS.md#L972-L973)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected the metadata-only 429 path. Previously queryFootprint() blocked the NAIP host, but no failedSources entry existed; needsUpdate()/recoverEligible() therefore never called retryHost() after Retry-After expired. The narrow fix calls markFailed('usgs-naip') on a footprint429 so it participates in the same guarded automatic recovery as tile/factory failures.

Regression reproduced RED: after a stationary footprint429 with Retry-After600, the query count stayed1 after600s. GREEN proves no retry at300s, one automatic request after600s, valid-footprint NAIP activation without another camera movement, and exactly one safety allocation. Existing concurrency/frequency/backoff/Retry-After gates and healthy native caches remain;401/403 stay closed.

The Earth artifact was rebuilt twice and independently byte-attested; installed/served512-file identity and focused unit/document/browser qualification are recorded in docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md under “Follow-up P2: footprint metadata429 recovery”. No source hierarchy, budget, upstream pin, Viewer, terrain or billing change.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle antimeridian-wrapped view rectangles**

When a close or regional view crosses ±180°, Cesium represents it with `west > east`; this check rejects that valid wrapped rectangle, so `chooseImagery()` always selects NASA even though EOX covers these Web Mercator longitudes. Users around Fiji, the Aleutians, or the Chukotka coast therefore remain on the 500 m overview rather than the automatic 10 m regional source; normalize or split wrapped rectangles before testing coverage.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L970-L973](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/f978491df2baf6dcad6c54b9006086e87c2c9af4/AGENTS.md#L970-L973)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected wrapped Cesium camera rectangles by splitting west>east at ±180 before testing coverage. Eligible regional/global views keep EOX rather than silently dropping to the500m NASA overview; wrapped views cannot accidentally qualify CONUS/PEMA. Polar/no-ground fallback remains safe.

Targeted policy regressions cover Fiji/Aleutians/full-longitude and wrapped-CONUS/polar refusal. Installed Chromium uses the actual pinned controller and native camera: both Fiji and Aleutian camera rectangles are verified west>east and automatically select EOX, with one safety base and one managed remote. No private controller fields, source pin, observer or camera ownership change.

The final exact-artifact performance/coverage qualification and remaining USGS/physical/owner gates are recorded in docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md under “C6-1A performance and automatic coverage correction — 2026-10-12”. PR stays unmerged.

Verified correction at `7b43d59cd80c9099938a23152d0b97ce13ed7f04`;91 Docker Earth tests,1 export,9 frontend,26 Docker document/artifact +36 subtests and14 installed-browser cases pass. Final Earth artifact `599dd5c6da6fbcdd22d3b2794639f1db31d9ca54a04c47cbfab31b9d9a66aaa3` is independently reproduced, installed/served byte-attested and bound to40 committed inputs.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the visible ground center for coverage queries**

For a tilted camera, `positionCartographic` is the camera eye's ellipsoid subpoint rather than the center of the visible ground area. It can be outside a PEMA/NAIP footprint while the displayed rectangle is inside it, causing `view()` to reject cached coverage and `queryFootprint()` to ask about the wrong coordinate; the covered view then stays on EOX until the camera returns near nadir. Derive this point by intersecting the viewport-center ray with the ellipsoid before making coverage decisions.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L970-L973](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/f978491df2baf6dcad6c54b9006086e87c2c9af4/AGENTS.md#L970-L973)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected coverage targeting to use the viewport-center ray's public globe intersection, with public ellipsoid picking before rendered tiles exist. The camera eye's geographic subpoint is no longer used as the query target. If no valid ground intersection exists, the wrapper keeps global imagery and issues no footprint request.

Regressions cover nadir/center-pixel ellipsoid fallback, tilted ground, finite grazing hit, no-ground/sky and stale camera/selection/lifecycle results. Camera-pose/extent identity prevents native mesh refinement alone from invalidating stationary metadata. Installed native-browser proof tilts an eye outside the PEMA boundary while its visible ground is covered and preserves automatic PEMA; sky-center mode selects NASA without a coverage query. Observer/camera execution and the pinned map controller remain unchanged.

The final exact-artifact performance/coverage qualification and remaining USGS/physical/owner gates are recorded in docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md under “C6-1A performance and automatic coverage correction — 2026-10-12”. PR stays unmerged.

Verified correction at `7b43d59cd80c9099938a23152d0b97ce13ed7f04`;91 Docker Earth tests,1 export,9 frontend,26 Docker document/artifact +36 subtests and14 installed-browser cases pass. Final Earth artifact `599dd5c6da6fbcdd22d3b2794639f1db31d9ca54a04c47cbfab31b9d9a66aaa3` is independently reproduced, installed/served byte-attested and bound to40 committed inputs.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close decoded tiles rejected as empty**

When `isEmpty` identifies a fully transparent NAIP tile, this branch rejects with a new error and discards the decoded `value` without calling its `close()` method. In browsers where Cesium returns `ImageBitmap` objects, repeatedly encountering no-data tiles can retain their graphics resources until garbage collection while Cesium retries or refines nearby tiles; close the rejected image before reporting the failure, as is already done for late successful resolutions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed at `ab2bae5e6fccc8c90c2d6470dfad728919e84ce5`. The guard safely disposes the decoded value before empty-tile rejection and before propagating an empty-detection exception. Accepted images remain open for Cesium. Late cancelled images close once, including empty/throwing detection; disposal exceptions cannot replace the original failure. Images without `close()` remain supported. Scheduling, counts, admission slots, promises, native errors and cancellation stay unchanged.

Regression-first proof: 18 request tests initially yielded 13 passes/5 expected disposal failures (close count 0 instead of 1). After correction: 52 focused request/controller/readiness tests, 98 final Docker Earth tests, one export-boundary check, nine frontend tests, type-check, 26 Docker document/artifact tests plus 36 subtests, and 14 installed desktop/mobile browser cases pass. Source-switch, cancellation and renderer teardown are included.

Earth was independently reproduced twice at `955cf90bce228d53ffeb1279cec693e1a906eb58625630048b43b1d5ac16caba`, bound to all 40 committed inputs, installed and byte-attested across all 512 served payload files. The previous performance gallery/candidate is preserved; four starts/sec and concurrency caps are unchanged. Existing read-only diagnostics now expose native tile state, monotonic time and actual fallback reason for owner hardware review. Actual owner-page ORAS smoke shows automatic PEMA/ready/native tiles loaded, recognizable detail and working normal zoom/pan; software rendering does not close physical acceptance.

Evidence and exact commands: `docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md`, section “C6-1A final decoded-image resource correction — 2026-10-12”. PR stays unmerged for owner review.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replay camera updates skipped during source preparation**

When the user moves the camera while a remote factory or NAIP readiness sample is pending, this early return discards the new `moveEnd` update because `updating` remains true across `await this.select(...)`. After the old selection completes, the timer will not correct it because `needsUpdate()` only checks footprint/cooldown recovery, not whether `desired(this.view())` differs from the active source. A slow NYC NAIP preparation followed by a move to Paris can therefore attach out-of-coverage NAIP for the old view and leave the stationary new view on the safety base until another camera movement; record a dirty update or rerun selection after the pending operation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L972-L976](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/ab2bae5e6fccc8c90c2d6470dfad728919e84ce5/AGENTS.md#L972-L976)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed at `9704054c0b4dcae5e1fb9f8306253cb4d3a8e196`. `updateView()` no longer serializes camera decisions behind a pending factory. The latest camera immediately issues the pinned controller's public `setStack` generation; stale update completions cannot run metadata follow-ups. Selecting the currently active source while a different source is pending also invalidates that pending choice. Same-source pending/healthy choices avoid redundant switches and preserve native caches.

The blocking two-tile NAIP readiness module/decoded holding cache is deleted, together with the Hub token bucket, start/concurrency caps, switching pauses and artificial tile/factory deadlines. Native Cesium dispatch/refinement/cancellation remains. Provider401/403/429/Retry-After and separately gated inactive ion financial authorization remain. A healthy verified PEMA view no longer qualifies the lower-quality NAIP fallback unnecessarily.

RED reproduced pending NYC→Paris ending on stale NAIP and20 native calls admitting only4. GREEN:103 Docker Earth/cache/lifecycle tests and16 installed desktop/mobile/browser/cache cases pass. Browser held-aerial tests move to Paris while NYC pixels are delayed, retain one safety/one remote and prove the latest source; teardown/Sky cycles and healthy upstream cache reuse pass. Public generation/provider metrics show one controller, two providers, generation2 after ORAS selection and unchanged counts/generation after zoom/revisit.

Final Earth `968d211328c14dac2b69fb0d302d8f70607de8d7a060ae8bcd5841631f99e4f0` is independently reproduced twice, bound to44 committed inputs and byte-attested over513 served payload files. Persistent response cache/confirmed owned clear is also qualified, including an actual browser restart, without credentials/opaque/no-store data or unrelated deletion. Exact commands/results and remaining native-provider/physical/owner gates are in docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md, “C6-1A native imagery dispatch and persistent cache — 2026-10-12”. PR remains unmerged for owner hardware/visual review.

Final qualification is now committed/pushed at35dcc94c1ecc1bdd87118d6dddb8b76fb81bbe9e. New camera intent immediately invokes the pinned controller public generation even while an older factory is pending; stale completions cannot run metadata follow-ups. Native latest-camera fixtures and installed desktop/mobile pending-provider scenarios pass.105 Docker Earth tests,16 installed browser cases; two independent builds and513 served files match current artifact7a8e04f6… with44 committed source inputs. The previous reply documents the original RED/GREEN correction. No merge or physical-device claim.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-run selection after caching a stale fallback**

When a source factory fails after its switch generation has become obsolete, the [pinned MapSourceController](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/e7707d9a0f34d9fbffc300023c319f95caa5be30/src/maps/controller.js#L166-L173) caches the fallback but deliberately skips subscriber notification for that generation. Consequently this branch does not add the failed source to `cachedFallbacks`; after cooldown, selecting that source resolves to the cached fallback, adds the marker only during that selection, and then remains there because `needsUpdate()` checks neither the new marker nor desired-versus-actual state. For example, a pending NAIP construction that fails after the camera moves to Paris will leave a later stationary return to covered NYC on EOX until another camera event; schedule a fresh selection when this newly discovered cached fallback matches the requested source.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L972-L973](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/9704054c0b4dcae5e1fb9f8306253cb4d3a8e196/AGENTS.md#L972-L973)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected in 35dcc94c1ecc1bdd87118d6dddb8b76fb81bbe9e. The pinned MapSourceController caches a successfully resolved construction fallback under the original source; a stale public setStack generation can skip the subscription that first exposes its marker. A regression reproduces pending NYC factory → Paris → rejected NYC factory → stationary NYC return: before the fix it remained EOX after cooldown. The existing health wake now checks whether the desired eligible source has a cached fallback and invokes the existing controlled public retry. This exceptional successful-fallback eviction uses public disposal/recreation because the pin has no single-cache detach API; normal switches and ordinary rejected factories keep healthy caches. No private fields, new polling loop, request caps or movement requirement. RED:1 expected failure; GREEN:105 Docker Earth tests,16 installed desktop/mobile/cache/navigation cases. Two independent builds and all513 served files match artifact7a8e04f6…;44 committed inputs verified. Evidence: docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md, native/cache review follow-up.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Purge expired entries while rebuilding the cache index**

When a cached tile expires without that exact URL being requested again, `index()` still counts it because it reads only size and insertion time and never checks `x-oras-cache-expires`. Such tiles can remain indefinitely, so diagnostics overstate usable entries and managed bytes, and quota calculations treat stale data as live until a later access happens to delete it. Validate expiry while indexing and remove expired records from CacheStorage so the owner-facing cache status and storage budget remain accurate.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L975-L978](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/9704054c0b4dcae5e1fb9f8306253cb4d3a8e196/AGENTS.md#L975-L978)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected in 35dcc94c1ecc1bdd87118d6dddb8b76fb81bbe9e. Index reconstruction now validates x-oras-cache-expires against the current clock and removes expired/invalid records from the owned cache before rebuilding entry/byte totals. The clear generation is checked before mutation. A regression advances the clock without requesting the cached URL again; before the fix status retained1 expired entry, after it reports0 entries/bytes and storage is purged. Foreground network dispatch and HTTP cache are unaffected. RED:1 expected failure; GREEN:105 Docker Earth tests,16 installed browser cases,26 document/artifact checks plus36 subtests. Independent builds/513 served files match artifact7a8e04f6… and44 committed inputs. Evidence: docs/validation/EARTH_HD_MAPPING_EVIDENCE.md, native/cache review follow-up.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind browser proof to the files being hashed**

When port 4200 is already serving another checkout or stale working tree, `DESIGN_PREVIEW_URL` directs all browser checks and screenshots to that server, while the ledger hashes files beside `verify.mjs`; the run can therefore report 16 passes and associate screenshots from one revision with source hashes from another. This is especially likely because the README tells reviewers to reuse the server if it is already running. Have the runner launch the preview from `root`, or fetch and compare every loaded source against the local bytes before recording proof.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L431-L448](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/b9650ef4824980f2532c99e30ee15c55760eb9d5/AGENTS.md#L431-L448)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore selected context when navigating back**

When a user selects the Moon in Solar System, approaches it, opens the Moon layout, and then uses Browser Back, this handler restores only the mode and calls `render()`; the selected body and open context panel existed only in the discarded DOM and are not stored or reapplied. The prior Solar view therefore loses the selection despite the reference promising that observer, time, and selection are preserved for return and the handoff saying the current view is kept. Persist the relevant design state in history and restore it on `popstate`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L431-L436](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/4c1e889683821f3fe79ab70fcbcd1704813fad07/AGENTS.md#L431-L436)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the Explore trigger across handoff cancellation**

When a user opens Explore, chooses a different destination, and then clicks “Stay here” or closes the handoff, `trigger` is the destination button inside the existing dialog. `openDialog()` records that button as `lastTrigger` and immediately replaces `modal.innerHTML`, disconnecting it, so `closeDialog()` cannot restore focus and focus falls outside the launcher instead of returning to Explore. Preserve the original connected Explore trigger when replacing one modal state with another.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L431-L436](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/4c1e889683821f3fe79ab70fcbcd1704813fad07/AGENTS.md#L431-L436)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return focus to the unavailable-state launcher**

When a user opens an Earth contextual-layer panel and activates “View unavailable state,” this branch calls `unavailable()` without passing `b`, so `openDialog()` retains the panel's earlier rail launcher as `lastTrigger`. Closing the unavailable dialog then moves focus out of the still-open panel instead of returning it to the button that launched the dialog, breaking the documented keyboard dismissal behavior; pass the connected launcher through to `openDialog()` and cover this nested-dialog path in the browser proof.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L431-L448](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/60e92336f7d715fc83d174f07ac350573d0e1953/AGENTS.md#L431-L448)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fresh evidence after the prior stale-preview fix shows that this ledger still hashes the earlier `reference.js` as `15c2bfe9…`, while the file in this commit hashes to `b1f8a272…`; it also records 19 checks although the revised runner adds two interaction groups. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve signed coordinate text during editing**

When a user clears a coordinate and types a leading `-` or an intermediate decimal separator, `valueAsNumber` is `NaN` or incomplete on that keystroke; storing it immediately causes React to rerender the controlled number input and discard the intermediate text. Consequently, southern/western coordinates and some decimal values cannot be entered normally by keyboard, even though the browser test's atomic `fill('-80')` succeeds. Keep draft fields as strings and parse and validate them only on submission.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L11-L18](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/4c1d58bb5cad2b6df56ee1586be55ed6db904bc7/AGENTS.md#L11-L18)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in `625376a0e24d26175e402077c27614bda67369d5`. Coordinate drafts now retain strings in text inputs and parse/validate only on submission. Real Chromium desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844 sequentially typed `-33.875`, `-80.125`, and `12.5`, then verified those actual native observer values. Partial, empty, malformed and out-of-range inputs caused zero observer writes; ORAS reset remained functional. Three focused draft tests and the complete 234-test frontend suite pass. [Exact-source browser evidence](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/r1-b-adaptive-sky-implementation-1/docs/validation/UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_IMPLEMENTATION_EVIDENCE.md#pr-74-sky-corrections--2026-10-14).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Synchronize fullscreen state when remounting Sky**

When a user enters whole-Hub fullscreen in Sky, switches to Earth through Explore without exiting fullscreen, and then returns to Sky, the parent `documentElement` remains fullscreen while the newly created Vue store starts with `fullscreen: false`. This mount only subscribes to future `fullscreenchange` events and never seeds the current state, so the Display action is mislabeled “Fullscreen” even though clicking it exits fullscreen. Invoke `onFullscreenChange` with the parent's current fullscreen state after registering the listener.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L11-L18](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/4c1d58bb5cad2b6df56ee1586be55ed6db904bc7/AGENTS.md#L11-L18)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in `625376a0e24d26175e402077c27614bda67369d5`. Mount registers the existing fullscreen listener and immediately calls it to seed native Vue state from the actual current fullscreen document. Real Chromium desktop/mobile retained whole-Hub fullscreen through two Earth/Sky round trips each; every remounted Sky reported fullscreen true and showed Exit fullscreen, then exited correctly. Parent listener count was one in Sky and zero after disposal to Earth. The focused mount regression and all observing-control regressions pass. [Exact-source browser evidence](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/r1-b-adaptive-sky-implementation-1/docs/validation/UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_IMPLEMENTATION_EVIDENCE.md#pr-74-sky-corrections--2026-10-14).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reattach fullscreen synchronization after bfcache restore**

On a top-level navigation that places Sky in the back-forward cache, `pagehide` has `persisted === true`, but this listener still calls `releaseFullscreen()` and there is no `pageshow` path that reattaches it. After Back restores the same Vue/frame instance, entering or exiting fullscreen no longer updates the native store, leaving the Display action mislabeled. This is separate from the remount issue: the fresh evidence is the unconditional `pagehide` cleanup without a restore counterpart; preserve the listener for cached departures or reinstall and reseed it on `pageshow`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L20-L23](https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/a01dfcf7993b6c0aac6cd7d1fa60b05cba30c0d3/AGENTS.md#L20-L23)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Corrected in `2811a511faa7daca42f1fce7a59a39bbeefed0eb`, delivered at `a57532796502a1db9ae1a7e4e4dc83e113db558f`. Persisted pagehide retains the existing single fullscreenchange listener; pageshow explicitly reseeds the native store from the current owning document. Genuine departure, renderer disposal and Vue destruction remove fullscreenchange/pageshow/pagehide/dispose ownership. No repeated listener installation occurs on resume.

Red/green regressions reproduced both stale resume state and lost subscription, then passed. They cover actual-state labels, three cached cycles with exactly one listener, one notification per change, genuine departure and explicit disposal. The complete runtime suite passes 48/48 with zero skips.

Actual Chromium was attempted against matching served source/artifact. The preview is excluded from bfcache (MainResourceHasCacheControlNoStore, JsNetworkRequestReceivedCacheControlNoStoreResource, BrowsingInstanceNotSwapped), so actual cached-return browser qualification is NOT_SUPPORTED and remains outstanding; no synthetic event or fresh load is claimed as cached proof. Resolving this source defect on deterministic red/green evidence, without claiming browser cache acceptance. Evidence and exact failure ledger: https://github.com/Shadowgar/Astronomy-Hub/blob/a57532796502a1db9ae1a7e4e4dc83e113db558f/docs/validation/UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_IMPLEMENTATION_EVIDENCE.md#pr-74-final-lifecycle-corrections--2026-10-14

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the lifecycle harness for the new night reporter**

Adding `installSkyNightReports()` here makes every evaluation of `entry.mjs` require that binding, but `tests/runtime/sky-page-lifecycle.test.mjs` strips imports and supplies only `installSkyPanelReports`. Running `node --test tests/runtime/*.test.mjs` now fails all six lifecycle cases with `ReferenceError: installSkyNightReports is not defined` before their assertions, eliminating the existing lifecycle regression coverage until the VM harness supplies the new reporter.

All six original lifecycle cases and their assertions are retained. Two added integration cases prove native Night reports survive repeated persisted departures and release all reporter-owned message/ready/night/pagehide listeners after genuine departure or explicit destroy; subsequent events cannot publish stale reports.

Reproduced the complete-suite failure first: 37 passed, 6 failed with the missing binding. Fresh `node --test tests/runtime/*.test.mjs`: all 11 files, 48 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
